title: Mississippi homeowners blame a noisy data center plant for sleepless nights. The mayor's advice? "Consider selling."
key_facts: Three residents of Southaven, Mississippi, who live within a mile of a plant powering Elon Musk's xAI data centers, sued xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech in June, alleging near-constant noise and vibrations are causing physical and psychological health effects.
Resident Jason Haley, 46, says the noise began around August 2025; he has recorded levels over 60 decibels as late as 10:15 p.m. in his backyard.

Mayor Darren Musselwhite acknowledged the noise as a problem in emails Haley shared with CBS and said he was working on a solution with xAI, but in a March email also advised Haley he 'may want to consider selling' his home; the mayor did not reply to CBS.
The mayor said in a February Facebook post that xAI spent millions on a sound wall, a berm and trees; a resident says it has not made a dent.
The NAACP sued xAI in April over pollution from the Southaven plant's gas turbines (27, since increased to 59 per a court filing) and has appealed the state's air permit for 41 permanent turbines.
Mississippi's governor's office puts Musk's investment in the area at $20 billion, calling it the largest economic development project in the state's history.
Similar noise lawsuits are reported in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, and Lowell, Massachusetts; the story carries no response from xAI.
quote_evidence: The noise keeping Haley awake was coming from a plant powering Elon Musk's xAI data centers in the area, according to a lawsuit filed in June against the company and its subsidiary, MZX Tech.
But in the same email, he offered Haley more advice: "I know they want houses for employees, so you may want to consider selling your home."
CBS News made multiple attempts to speak with Musselwhite and did not receive a reply.
why_it_matters_hint: Residents near a power plant built for AI data centers say the noise harms their sleep and health, and their mayor's reply has become part of the story.
event_date: CBS report published 5 Oct 2026; the lawsuit was filed in June 2026 and the emails date from November 2025 to March 2026.
notes: The health claims are allegations in a lawsuit. The story carries no response from xAI. New reporting by CBS (emails shared by a resident) on an older dispute, so it is treated as new.
